raw_response:
I'm fifty years old and I've worked these 3 mu for thirty years. It's just me and my wife now — our son works in Shijiazhuang — so every decision has to be something two people can manage without hiring too much help. We've always done wheat-maize double cropping, and I don't see any reason to change. This land is all we have, and I can't afford a bad year.

Right now it's autumn and I'm getting ready to plant winter wheat after the maize comes off. I'll hire the rotary tiller to work the stubble under — costs about 30 yuan per mu, but my back isn't what it used to be and the soil needs a fine seedbed for wheat. I'm using the same improved wheat seed I've used for years; I know it, it germinates well here, and the dealer in town always has it. For fertilizer, I'll put down 40 kg of compound fertilizer per mu at planting, then topdress with urea at jointing and again at heading. The extension fellow says 15 kg of nitrogen per mu is enough, but three years ago I tried cutting back and my yield dropped by nearly 80 jin per mu. With only 3 mu, I can't take that risk. I'd rather spend the extra 100 yuan on fertilizer than lose half a mu's worth of grain. So I figure I'm putting about 18 kg of nitrogen, 6 kg of phosphorus, and 5 kg of potassium per mu. I'll irrigate three times from the well: once after planting to settle the seed, once at jointing in March, and once at heading in April. The electricity bill hurts, but wheat won't fill its heads without water. Two sprays: herbicide in early spring, and insecticide if I see aphids.

For summer maize next year, the window between wheat harvest and maize planting is maybe five days. I'll plant hybrid seed directly into the wheat stubble with a no-tillage planter — I hire Old Wang from the next village who has the machine. No time for tillage, and anyway the stubble helps keep moisture in July. I'll band compound fertilizer at planting and side-dress urea when the maize is at the big trumpet stage — that's about 16 kg nitrogen, 5 kg phosphorus, and 4 kg potassium per mu. If the summer rains are normal, I only need to irrigate once at flowering. Last year I didn't irrigate at all and the ears were small, so this year I'm budgeting for one watering. Two pesticide applications: pre-emergence herbicide, and one spray for corn borer in August.

I expect about 500 kg per mu for wheat and 550 kg per mu for maize if the weather is fair. That's enough for our household grain and some cash from selling the surplus. I know I could probably save a little on fertilizer, but at my age with only 3 mu, stability matters more than squeezing every last yuan.
